QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.520 on November 6 to 0.455 on November 13, below the independent finite-variance reference, 0.5. R²=0.936 measures fit only across supplied scales. Short/long H=0.393/0.648 indicates one straight-line exponent fits poorly across scales 8–63: possibly crossover or transient volatility change, not clean scaling.

H changed −0.024/−0.065 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-only 30-observation standardized deviation is −1.33; overlapping windows preclude significance testing. Magnitude DFA-1 H=0.759 suggests stronger volatility clustering than signed returns near 0.5, not tradable predictability.

Hill alpha rose 3.300→3.380 over those dates, using 1,000 returns (~four years), k=100, x_min=0.02018 absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner fitted tails under a suitable model. Plateaus are normal when new returns miss the top k, not evidence of stasis. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SOXX.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
SOXX’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.491 on 2026-11-06 to 0.416 on 2026-11-13, below the independent finite-variance reference 0.5. R²=0.910 measures fit only over scales 8–63. Short/long H=0.347/0.662 means one straight-line exponent fits poorly: possible crossover or transient volatility shift, not one clean scaling law.

H changed −0.028/−0.075 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-only 30-observation standardized deviation is −1.88; overlapping windows prevent significance-test interpretation. DFA-1 of magnitudes gives h_abs=0.771, a stronger volatility-clustering contrast, not tradable predictability.

Hill alpha fell from 3.066 to 2.985 over those dates: lower/higher means heavier/thinner fitted absolute-return tails, conditional on a suitable model. Its separate 1,000-return window uses k=99, x_min=0.038645 absolute log-return units. Alpha/√k=0.300 is an idealized i.i.d. standard error, understating uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.297/2.579, not a confidence interval. Unchanged alpha since November 12 can reflect new returns missing the top 99; such order-statistic plateaus do not mean a static market. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
